newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mutual funds post positive returns in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Israel mutual funds post positive returns in Sept.

text.p: Israeli mutual funds averaged returns of 2.6 percent in September, as the stock and bond markets rallied most of the month, according to the Meitav investment and research house.
The rise in Meitav's mutual fund index was led by flexible funds, which hold stocks and bonds, and posted average positive yields of 3.1 percent. Stock funds had positive yields of 2.8 percent.

The funds nevertheless lagged the market. The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's General Share Index rose 3.6 percent in September, despite sharp declines in the final days of the month in response to the violent clashes between Israelis and Palestinians.
Although stock and bond prices began to recover in mid-August, they are down for the year - a fact reflected in the mutual funds' performance for the first nine months.

Meitav's mutual fund index fell 1.3 percent in the January to September period. Only 55 of 302 surveyed funds showed positive returns after inflation. Stock funds have been by far the worst performers, with negative returns of 14.9 percent so far this year.
